wheel.note: Cruiser Corps lists the same 15x5.5 OEM steel wheel for 1958–1990 FJ40, FJ45, FJ55, FJ60, FJ62 and BJ trucks, and advises against tires wider than 10.5 in on it.

max_tire.note: Corsetti runs 31x10.50s on stock springs. IH8MUD owners run 33x9.50s unlifted, but 33x12.50s won't fit without a lift.
Corsetti's setup. One IH8MUD owner fits 34x10.5 KO2s on a heavy-duty OME kit. Corsetti says don't go wider than 10.5 in or taller than 33 in on a factory rim, and fit a steering damper.
35s rub on a 2.5-inch OME kit alone. IH8MUD owners add a body lift, shackle or spring changes, or about 4 inches of lift.

items.title: Steering tie rod can fracture
items.summary: Sustained driving over 50 mph on very rough roads can resonate and crack the tie rod; Toyota replaced the tie rod and relay rod free.

items.title: Rear lap belt may not retract
items.summary: The rear lap belt can stay partly extended and lock; the fix was a belt guide or sheath.

items.title: Fuel tank welds can crack
items.summary: Heat and load can pressurize the tank and crack its welds, leaking fuel that can catch fire near an ignition source; the remedy was an improved tank (38,500 vehicles).

timeline.change: 60 Series introduced with A/C, a rear heater and a nicer cabin; the US gets the 2F carbureted six and a four-speed for 1981
Tie-rod recall on 1981 trucks; a high-roof version is introduced
Five-speed H55F arrives in other markets (Wikipedia; Toyota UK says 1983); US trucks keep the four-speed
Most markets get the 4.0 L 3F; North America keeps the 2F
April 1985 running change: the H42 gets a spacer that makes later trucks H55F-ready, and suspension parts split (OME kits fit 4/1985–1/1990); HJ61 12H-T turbodiesel launched abroad
Last US FJ60 model year; the FJ62 replaces it for 1988

identify.intro: Plenty of '60s for sale' are FJ62s, imported diesels or five-speed conversions. Know what the US FJ60 actually came with.

items.head: US drivetrain
items.body: US FJ60s had the 4.2 L 2F carbureted six and a four-speed H41F/H42F, a gearbox Toyota sold only in the US. A five-speed US truck has been converted.

items.head: Altitude system
items.body: 1981–87 US trucks have High Altitude Compensation emissions gear that works above 3,930 ft. A Weber carb means that system has been bypassed.

items.head: Build date split
items.body: Suspension and other parts change at April 1985 production. Check the build date before ordering springs or a lift kit.

items.head: FJ60 vs FJ62
items.body: The FJ60 is the pre-facelift truck with round headlights and a carburetor. The FJ62 (1988–90) has square headlights, the fuel-injected 3F-E and an automatic.

items.head: Diesels
items.body: BJ60, HJ60 and HJ61 diesels and the FJ61 with the 3F were never sold new in the US. US-titled examples are imports.

capability.v: 184 x 70.9 x 69.5 in (L x W x H)

values.intro: Clean, rust-free FJ60s keep climbing as the analog alternative to an 80, and rust decides most of the price.
values.note: Based on 100 Bring a Trailer sales of FJ60s and 60 Series diesels from January 2025 to October 2026 (median about $29,100). Top results include an $85,000 42-years-family-owned 1982 FJ60, an $80,000 HJ61 turbodiesel and $69,000–79,000 Cummins R2.8 swaps.

paragraphs: The US got only the gasoline FJ60 (1981–87) and FJ62 (1988–90). BJ60, HJ60 and HJ61 diesels, high-roof wagons and FJ61s are gray-market. Japanese 60 Series production ended in 1990 and Venezuelan production in 1992, so every 60 is now more than 25 years old, which NHTSA measures from the date of manufacture. Corsetti Cruisers warns that California may refuse to register an import without a 50-state-compliant emissions system, so check your state's rules before buying an HJ61.

production.intro: The 60 Series was built in Japan from 1980 to 1990, with Venezuelan assembly to 1992.

items.v: Land Cruiser sales passed 1 million in 1981

production.paint: 60 Series colors were Alpine White, Brown, Desert Beige, Freeborn Red and Royal Blue, plus metallic Charcoal Gray, Cognac, Gray-Blue, Rootbeer, Sky Blue and Stardust Silver.
